data.name: Chamanlal
data.gender_notes: Chamanlal is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Chamanlal is derived from Sanskrit words ‘Chama’ and ‘Lal’. Chama means ‘God’ and Lal means ‘servant’. Thus, Chamanlal translates to ‘God’s servant’. This name is used to denote a devout and religious person who dedicates his life to the service of God. The name Chamanlal carries the meaning “God's servant” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Chamanlal usually hope their child will grow to embody god's servant and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Living a life devoted to the divine
data.etymology: Chamanlal belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “God's servant.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Chamanlal total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

in_sanskrit.name: चामनलल
in_sanskrit.meaning: पूजा करना, सेवा करना (To serve, to worship)
in_sanskrit.long_meaning: च (Cha) - to serve, आमन (Aman) - to please, लल (Lal) - to play or enjoy. Thus, Chamanlal means one who serves, pleases and enjoys the divine.

in_hindi.name: चामनलल
in_hindi.long_meaning: च (Cha) - to serve, म (Ma) - mother, न (Na) - in, ल (La) - to serve, ल (La) - to serve. Thus, Chamanlal is a name that signifies serving and pleasing the divine as well as one's mother.

in_tamil.name: சாமனலல்
in_tamil.long_meaning: ச (Ca) - to serve, ஆட்டு (Attu) - always, கள் (Kal) - to hold or possess, அளிவத்துவம் (Aalivaththuvam) - serving attitude. Thus, Chamanlal in Tamil means one with a constant serving attitude.

in_telugu.name: చామనలల్
in_telugu.long_meaning: చ (Cha) - to serve, ఆ (Aa) - always, మ (Ma) - mother, న (Na) - in, ల (La) - to serve, ల (La) - to serve. Thus, Chamanlal in Telugu means a constant God-loving servant.

historical_references.reference: Chamanlal was a prominent Jain businessman and philanthropist from Bikaner, Rajasthan in the late 19th and early 20th centuries. He was known for his contributions to Jainism and education.
